title: Partitions of Poland
summary: Weak against its neighbours, the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth was carved up by Russia, Prussia and Austria in three steps. The first partition, agreed on 5 August 1772, left a smaller Poland still standing. Reforms that culminated in the liberal constitution of 1791 alarmed Russia and Prussia, which sent troops and took more land in the second partition of 1793. After crushing a Polish revolt in 1794, the three powers divided what remained on 24 October 1795, and Poland vanished from the map of Europe until 1918.

uncertainty.note: First partition treaty signed 5 August 1772; third partition concluded 24 October 1795.
